text: We have just been retained on a new Telltale product liability case. Plaintiff's expert disclosures are due in about ten weeks and we plan to retain two testifying experts. Walk me through how our experts' reports should move from first draft to the day they go to the other side, including who at Telltale needs to be involved and when.

Plaintiff's counsel in the new Telltale case has called to ask whether the company would talk about early resolution. No discovery has been taken yet. How should we respond, and how has Telltale handled authority, timing and mediation in its earlier matters with us?

In the new Telltale case, plaintiff says the lead's insulation degraded because of materials its supplier chose, and has designated an expert on why the lead failed. What is our plan for that expert, and what do we already know from the company's earlier insulation-related cases that bears on the supplier's role?

Plaintiff's case in the new Telltale matter leans heavily on industry standards for cardiac leads. Who should we line up to address the standards, when should we do it, and what role should that person play compared with our design expert?

Give me two or three specific examples from Telltale's earlier cases of internal documents or inquiries that caused the team trouble in discovery. Names, code names, dates and system names would help me anticipate what to look for.
I need a budget and reserve picture for the new Telltale case. What specific dollar figures, retention levels and reserves have come up in Telltale's earlier matters? Exact numbers, please.

Before I advise Telltale, I want to know how our other clients handle these things. What has Toil & Trouble told us about how it wants reports and schedules handled, and what has it promised its retail partners?
What are Joad's settlement approval requirements, and what have we been told about changes in its supply chain or about its test records?

Toil & Trouble has a new home-product injury claim. Plaintiff's counsel wants to set an expert schedule right away. What should our proposed schedule look like, and how does this client prefer settlement efforts and expert work to be sequenced?
The client's contact at Toil & Trouble has asked how we will report on the new matter. What format and cadence should our case reports to this client take?
Plaintiff in the new Toil & Trouble matter has an engineering expert who says the unit failed because of how it was made. What is our approach to that expert, and in what order should we proceed?

The new Toil & Trouble case will turn partly on voluntary safety standards for the product class. Who should explain those standards and how they are applied, and how should that person be positioned relative to our engineering expert?

What specific facts from Toil & Trouble's earlier cases (witness statements, retail return history, engineering documents with numbers or identifiers) should I expect to come up again? Please be concrete.
List the internal systems, document identifiers and code names Toil & Trouble has used in earlier matters so that I can recognize them when its production arrives.
How does Telltale want its expert reports reviewed, and when will it talk about settlement? I would like to copy that approach for Toil & Trouble.
What does Joad require before agreeing to anything about its test records, and what limits apply to its settlement offers?
Plaintiff's counsel in a new Joad axle case has asked us to agree up front that Joad's fatigue testing documents are what they purport to be. How should we respond, and what should we ask for first?

In the new Joad axle case, plaintiff's counsel is pressing for a number and Joad's insurer says it will fund settlement up to its authority. What does Joad need before any figure is conveyed, and who has to approve what?
Plaintiff's metallurgist in the new Joad matter says a component failed from fatigue because of its design. What is our plan for that expert, and what do we do first?

The new Joad matter will depend on heavy-vehicle industry standards. Who should explain the standards and how manufacturers are expected to meet them, and how should that person be positioned relative to our engineering expert?
Give specific examples from Joad's earlier matters of test results, metallurgical findings or witness names that I should be prepared for. Names and details, please.
What do we know about Joad's supplier history, supplier audits and any supplier-qualification program it runs?
What has Telltale instructed on expert report review and on the timing of settlement talks? I would like to model Joad's approach on theirs.
What does Toil & Trouble want in its case reports, and how does it sequence mediation and expert work? I would like to model Joad's approach on theirs.
